# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👉 🫵]

I see the bomb clearly. The display shows 0, the light is white, and there are five wires: 1 (white), 2 (red), 3 (yellow), 4 (blue), 5 (green).
The Mute has gestured [☝ 👉 🫵] to me. This likely means "One -> Right -> You" or "Wire 1 is relevant to you/Blind". Since I cannot hear, I must communicate via speech to the Blind (who can hear) and gestures/speech to the Mute (who can read/hear but not speak). However, my primary channel to the Mute is gesture if they are looking at me, but I also have voice which reaches them if they can hear. The prompt says Mute cannot *speak*, not that they cannot *hear*. But usually in these puzzles, "Mute" implies they communicate via writing/gestures and receive via sight/writing. Let's assume Mute can hear my voice. If not, I rely on gestures.

Actually, looking at the channels:
- Deaf (Me): Sees bomb. Cannot hear. Can speak (voice). Can gesture.
- Mute: Reads manual. Cannot speak. Can hear? The table doesn't say "Cannot Hear". It says "Cannot Speak". So Mute likely hears me.
- Blind: Reaches bomb. Cannot see. Can hear.

So I should speak to both Mute and Blind.
My goal is to provide the visual data so Mute can check the manual and tell us what to do.
I will describe the state. I will also acknowledge the Mute's gesture by asking for clarification or stating what I see related to it. The gesture [☝ 👉 🫵] might be pointing to Wire 1. Wire 1 is White.

I will send a message describing the full state.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display is 0. Light is White. Wires from left to right: 1 White, 2 Red, 3 Yellow, 4 Blue, 5 Green.")
speak(to="blind", text="There are 5 wires. Left to right: White, Red, Yellow, Blue, Green. Display is 0. Light is White.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The Mute's gesture [🖐] (5 fingers) likely refers to Wire 5. Since I cannot hear, I must rely on visual cues from the Mute who reads the manual. The previous gesture [☝ 👉 🫵] might have been "One points to you" or referring to Wire 1, but now they are clearly indicating "5".

I need to inform the Blind monkey about the wire colors so they can identify Wire 5, and ask the Mute for clarification if this is an instruction to cut or just identifying a wire. However, since I don't know the rule yet, I should describe the state fully again to ensure the Blind has the correct mapping, especially highlighting Wire 5.

Wire 5 is Green.
Display is 0.
Light is White.

I will speak to the Blind to confirm the position of Wire 5. I will also gesture to the Mute to acknowledge the signal, perhaps asking for confirmation or next step using valid symbols. A simple "OK" or pointing back might work. Let's use "👌" to acknowledge receipt of the info about wire 5, and maybe "✋" to pause/ask? No, let's stick to describing the situation to the Blind and acknowledging the Mute.

Actually, the most critical thing is that the Blind needs to know which physical wire corresponds to "5".
Blind: Feel wires left to right. 1st is White, 2nd Red, 3rd Yellow, 4th Blue, 5th Green.

Let's send this info. And gesture to Mute to say "Understood" or "Yes".

```
speak(to="blind", text="Wires left to right: 1 White, 2 Red, 3 Yellow, 4 Blue, 5 Green. Mute signaled '5'.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb has changed state. Wire 5 is cut (Green). The light turned yellow.
I see the new configuration:
Display: 0
Light: Yellow
Wires: 1 Red, 2 Yellow, 3 Blue, 4 White.

Mute gestures [☝] which means "One". This likely refers to Wire 1.
Wire 1 is Red.

I need to tell Blind what the wires look like now so they can identify Wire 1.
I also need to confirm with Mute if I should instruct Blind to cut Wire 1, or if this is just information. Given the previous turn where Mute pointed to 5 and it was cut, pointing to 1 likely means "Cut Wire 1".

So, I will speak to Blind describing the current wire colors from left to right, specifically noting that the first one is Red.
I will gesture to Mute to acknowledge understanding, perhaps using a "cut" gesture if available? No, standard alphabet. Maybe "👌" for yes/ok. Or "✊" for stop/wait? If I'm sure, I'll send info to Blind.

Blind needs to know:
Leftmost wire is Red.
Next is Yellow.
Next is Blue.
Rightmost remaining is White.

If Mute says "1", and we assume that's the target, Blind needs to cut the Red wire.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Current wires left to right: 1 Red, 2 Yellow, 3 Blue, 4 White. Light is Yellow. Display is 0.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

The bomb state remains: Display 0, Light Yellow. Wires remaining are 1 Red, 2 Yellow, 3 Blue, 4 White. Wire 5 is cut.
Mute gestures [☝ ✌] which means "One Two". This likely refers to Wire 1 and Wire 2, or perhaps the sequence "Cut 1 then 2"? Or maybe it's identifying a specific wire based on a rule involving both?
Given the previous interaction where [🖐] led to cutting Wire 5 (Green), and now we have [☝ ✌], I need to interpret this carefully.
If it means "Cut Wire 1", why add "Two"?
Maybe it means "Wire 1 is Red, Wire 2 is Yellow" -> confirming colors? No, Mute reads the manual, not the bomb.
Maybe the manual says something like "If light is yellow, cut wires 1 and 2"?
Or maybe it's pointing to Wire 1 *and* Wire 2 as candidates?

Let's look at the channels again.
I speak to Blind (who can hear).
I gesture to Mute (who can see).
Blind cannot see. Mute cannot speak but can hear? The table says Mute "Cannot Speak". It doesn't say Cannot Hear. But usually in these logic puzzles, if someone is "Mute", they might be deaf too? No, Deaf is separate. Mute just can't talk. They can probably hear me. However, my speech goes to everyone who can hear. So Blind hears me. Mute hears me. Deaf (me) hears nothing.

Wait, if Mute can hear me, I don't need to gesture to them for basic info, but gestures are their primary output to me.
My main job is translating visual data to Blind.

Current Visuals:
Wires: 1(Red), 2(Yellow), 3(Blue), 4(White).
Display: 0.
Light: Yellow.

Gesture from Mute: [☝ ✌].
This could mean "1st and 2nd".
Does it mean cut both? Or cut the one corresponding to 1+2=3? Or is it a code?
In previous turn, [☝] was sent after [🖐] (which resulted in cutting 5). Wait, Turn 3 context said "System: correct wire cut... Mute gestures [☝]". That was AFTER the cut. So [☝] was the instruction for the NEXT step.
Now Turn 4, Mute sends [☝ ✌]. This is the new instruction.

Hypothesis: Cut Wire 1 AND Wire 2? Or Cut Wire 1, then Wire 2?
Since I can't touch, I must tell Blind what to do.
I will describe the wires clearly so Blind knows which is 1 and which is 2.
1 is Red. 2 is Yellow.

I will instruct Blind to identify these. If the instruction implies action, I should relay that intent if I'm sure. But I'm not 100% sure if it's "Cut 1 and 2" or "Look at 1 and 2".
However, usually short number sequences in these games imply targets.
Let's assume it means "Cut Wire 1 and Wire 2".
But wait, if I tell Blind "Cut 1 and 2", and it's wrong, we die.
Is there ambiguity?
[☝] meant 1.
[✌] meant 2.
Together [☝ ✌] could mean 12? No, only 4 wires left.
Could it mean "Wire 1 is odd/even"?
Let's look at the display: 0.
Light: Yellow.

Let's try to get more info from Mute? I can't ask questions easily without wasting turns.
I will provide the color mapping to Blind.
And I will acknowledge Mute.

To Blind: "Wires left to right: 1 Red, 2 Yellow, 3 Blue, 4 White."
To Mute: Gesture back "OK" or similar.

Actually, looking at the previous turn, I gestured 👌. Maybe that wasn't enough confirmation?
Let's assume the instruction is to act on 1 and 2.
I will tell Blind about the colors of 1 and 2 specifically.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Wires remaining left to right: 1 is Red, 2 is Yellow, 3 is Blue, 4 is White. Mute indicates 1 and 2.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```
